target_profile.system_boundary: The github.com/hashicorp/raft library, including its protocol workers and in-repository adapter implementations. Client FSM logic and separately maintained storage backends are outside the concrete code currently supplied; constructor injection does not exclude built-in implementations from the inventory.
protocol_contexts: Leader-local commitment instance with startIndex and voter match indexes
Snapshot index, term, configuration and publication state
external_interfaces: Apply, ApplyLog, Barrier and VerifyLeader futures
FSM, optional BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore callbacks
Transport RPC channel, optional heartbeat fast path and optional WithPreVote
ownership: NewRaft assembles caller-provided adapters and starts run, runFSM and runSnapshots unless skipStartup is set.
The main thread owns configuration information requested by takeSnapshot through configurationsCh.
runFSM owns local lastIndex and lastTerm used for snapshot capture.
commitment serializes match-index and commit-index access with a mutex.
The transport may execute the registered heartbeat handler concurrently with a blocking RPC.
selection_injection: NewRaft receives Config, FSM, LogStore, StableStore, SnapshotStore and Transport.
BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore support are selected through runtime interface assertions.
Pre-vote is disabled by configuration or lack of WithPreVote support.
FileSnapshotSink is an acquired built-in implementation; its activation in a concrete deployment is unknown.
The file catalogue also identifies in-memory, discard, cache and network implementation files; their behavior and selection remain unread.
variants: Buffered versus unbuffered applyCh through BatchApplyCh
Pre-vote versus direct election, including leadership-transfer bypass
Protocol versions below 2 encode configuration changes using deprecated peer entries
File snapshot synchronization depends on noSync and operating system
unknowns: Actual deployment configuration and selected adapter instances
Built-in log and stable store failure semantics
Complete startup restore, follower resynchronization and user restore paths
Future completion synchronization and payload ownership

activities.purpose: Store proposed logs, aggregate replication support and advance local decision state.
activities.realization_summary: Leader dispatch stores logs before reporting local match. commitment computes a quorum order statistic over current voter reports and advances only at or above startIndex. The remote report producers and decision consumer remain unread.

activities.purpose: Acquire and change authority and election context.
activities.realization_summary: runCandidate tallies pre-vote and vote results, processes RPCs, handles election timeout and rejects leader-only requests. Vote production and persistent election state are not recovered.

activities.purpose: Reconstruct participant state and restore snapshots.
activities.realization_summary: Startup loads term and last log, attempts snapshot restoration and scans later configuration entries. The FSM worker has a separate restore closure. Complete recovery and resumption are deferred.

appendConfigurationEntry derives a configuration, dispatches its log, installs latest configuration, replaces commitment voters and adjusts replication. Admission and committed-configuration transitions remain unread.

activities.purpose: Process decision tuples through application callbacks and complete their futures.
activities.realization_summary: runFSM implements single and batch callback paths and tracks snapshot coordinates. Concrete client state transitions are external; library scheduling and filtering are internal.

activities.purpose: Persist logs and snapshots and reclaim retained history.
activities.realization_summary: takeSnapshot obtains FSM capture and committed configuration, persists and closes a sink, records snapshot coordinates and compacts logs. FileSnapshotSink implements finalization, rename, optional directory sync and retention cleanup.

activities.purpose: Admit client operations and communicate completion or failure.
activities.realization_summary: ApplyLog and Barrier return futures after channel enqueueing or immediate timeout/shutdown errors. VerifyLeader has a separate request channel. API comments distinguish leadership-loss uncertainty from restore-aborted writes.

behaviors.execution_owner: Client goroutine invoking ApplyLog or Barrier
behaviors.protocol_context: One Raft instance and newly allocated logFuture
legal_preconditions: API documentation requires a leader for successful execution; enqueueing itself does not check role.
implementation_guards: Select between timer, shutdownCh and applyCh send
writes: Fresh LogCommand or LogBarrier future without assigned index or term
external_effects: Returns queued future or immediate errorFuture
important_branches: Positive timeout enables timer
Timeout and shutdown return errors
Successful send returns the same future
async_boundaries: applyCh send precedes later protocol handling
unknowns: Leader acceptance and subsequent future resolution
Caller mutation of submitted byte slices

behaviors.protocol_context: Current term, last log index and leaderState
legal_preconditions: Function is described as leader-only; callers beyond configuration dispatch are unread.
implementation_guards: Checks StoreLogs error before local match and last-log update
durable_effects: Calls LogStore.StoreLogs; actual durability depends on the selected implementation
external_effects: Responds with storage error on failure
important_branches: Storage failure responds to all submitted futures, sets Follower and returns
Storage success reports local match before updating last-log metadata

cross_activity_effects.A1: Reports the last assigned index to commitment.match after StoreLogs returns nil.

existing_protections: No local match report after a non-nil StoreLogs result

behaviors.execution_owner: Caller of commitment.match under the commitment mutex
behaviors.protocol_context: One commitment instance and its current voter map
legal_preconditions: The comment requires a completed write and agreement through matchIndex; remote callers establishing this are unread.
implementation_guards: Server must exist in voter map
Reported index must strictly exceed stored index
important_branches: Unknown voter and non-increasing reports are ignored
Advancement requires quorumMatchIndex greater than commitIndex and at least startIndex
unknowns: Local store fact is a prerequisite of the observed local caller, not every match invocation

behaviors.execution_owner: Caller of commitment.setConfiguration under the commitment mutex
behaviors.protocol_context: Existing commitment instance and supplied configuration
legal_preconditions: Configuration eligibility is determined by unread upstream validation and admission.
implementation_guards: Only Voter entries populate the replacement map
important_branches: Retained voter IDs preserve reports
New voter IDs start at zero
Empty voter map causes recalculation to return

cross_activity_effects.A1: Changes the voter set used for subsequent quorum-index calculation and immediately recalculates.

existing_protections: Existing commit index is not reduced
unknowns: Meaning of retained reports across membership histories

behaviors.protocol_context: Latest configuration, configuration request and protocol version
legal_preconditions: Leader admission and outstanding configuration restrictions are unread.
durable_effects: Invokes dispatchLogs for configuration entry storage
important_branches: Protocol version below 2 uses deprecated peer encoding
After dispatchLogs returns, proceeds to configuration updates without an explicit error test in this function
async_boundaries: Replication work initiated through called helpers

cross_activity_effects.A1: Supplies the newly derived configuration to the commitment aggregator.

unknowns: Effects of dispatch failure on subsequent configuration updates

behaviors.protocol_context: One commitTuple and current FSM instance
behaviors.trigger: Single application path processes a tuple
legal_preconditions: Tuple commitment and ordering are attributed to interface comments; the producer is unread.
writes: Worker lastIndex and lastTerm except unsupported configuration early return
durable_effects: Application callback persistence is external and unknown
external_effects: Invokes FSM.Apply for commands or StoreConfiguration for supported configurations
important_branches: Unsupported LogConfiguration returns before coordinate update while deferred future response still runs
Other types execute no application callback and update coordinates

cross_activity_effects.A7: Stores the callback response in the associated future and requests successful completion.
cross_activity_effects.A6: Updates coordinates later used by the FSM snapshot closure.

behaviors.protocol_context: One tuple batch and BatchingFSM instance
behaviors.trigger: Batch application path processes tuples with batching enabled
legal_preconditions: Commitment and ordering of input tuples require the unread producer.
implementation_guards: Only commands and configurations enter ApplyBatch
Response count must equal callback input count
writes: Worker coordinates from final input tuple
durable_effects: Application callback persistence is external and unknown
external_effects: Calls ApplyBatch when filtered input is nonempty
Requests successful completion of present futures
important_branches: Barriers are filtered from callback input
Response count mismatch panics
No callback for an empty filtered batch

cross_activity_effects.A7: Assigns responses by position among callback-eligible logs before completing futures.
cross_activity_effects.A6: Tracks the final tuple coordinate even when that tuple is filtered from the callback.

existing_protections: Common filtering predicate during dispatch and response assignment
unknowns: Cross-path significance of differing configuration coordinate handling

behaviors.protocol_context: Current FSM and worker-local lastIndex and lastTerm
writes: Request snapshot object, index and term
external_effects: Calls FSM.Snapshot and responds with its error
important_branches: No processed coordinate returns ErrNothingNewToSnapshot
Capture error is propagated
async_boundaries: Snapshot future response to snapshot worker
unknowns: Whether client snapshot object faithfully represents those coordinates

behaviors.protocol_context: One capture request, later configuration response and selected SnapshotStore
legal_preconditions: Snapshot scheduling and caller serialization are unread.
implementation_guards: Checks capture and configuration future errors
Requires capture index at least committed configuration index
Checks Create, Persist and Close errors before updating snapshot coordinates
durable_effects: Invokes log compaction after updating snapshot coordinates
external_effects: Returns sink ID on complete success
important_branches: Persist error invokes Cancel and returns
Close error returns before coordinate update
Compaction error returns after coordinate update

cross_activity_effects.A3: Requests creation of a snapshot carrying FSM and committed-configuration coordinates for later recovery.

existing_protections: Persistence and close checks precede compaction

behaviors.protocol_context: One file sink with closed flag, temporary directory and synchronization options
legal_preconditions: Concurrent calls and prior Persist behavior require caller and interface review.
implementation_guards: Returns nil immediately if closed is already true
Checks finalize, metadata write, rename, optional directory sync and reaping errors
durable_effects: Flushes state, optionally syncs state file, closes it, writes metadata and renames directory
external_effects: Returns an error from failed processing
Attempts temporary directory removal after finalize failure
important_branches: Repeated Close returns nil without revisiting earlier processing
A first Close may fail before or after rename
Parent directory sync is skipped on Windows or with noSync
unknowns: How client Persist handles a Close error
Whether a subsequent nil Close is consumed after a failed first Close

facts.meaning: The newly created command or barrier future was successfully sent to this instance's applyCh. This establishes enqueueing, not leader acceptance, storage, commitment or application.
facts.validity_context: Successful applyCh branch of ApplyLog or Barrier.
facts.recovery: No recovery of queued requests is established.

facts.meaning: The selected LogStore returned nil for the assigned leader log batch. Durable persistence is not established without adapter semantics.
facts.durability: A storage API result; crash durability remains adapter-dependent.
facts.recovery: Startup reads stored logs, but storage survival and complete reconstruction are unresolved.
unknowns: Local commitment reporting occurs in the producer; no generic match consumer edge is asserted

facts.meaning: At an advancement event, the quorum order statistic of the current voter report map exceeded the previous commitIndex and met startIndex. This is an assertion about recorded reports, not independently verified remote disk contents.

identity.advancement: New commitIndex and voter map at recalculation

facts.validity_context: Mutex-held recalculation reaching its assignment branch through match or setConfiguration.
facts.recovery: Constructor creates a new commitment instance; restart and leadership lifecycle callers are unread.
unknowns: Later configurations need not have the same quorum statistic

facts.meaning: For a command tuple, the selected single or batch FSM callback returned and its corresponding result was assigned to a present future before successful completion was requested.
facts.validity_context: Normal callback return; batch execution also passed its response-length check.
facts.durability: Callback-return event; application persistence is unspecified.
facts.recovery: No recovery of future results is shown.

facts.meaning: FSM.Snapshot returned without error and the request carries its object with the worker's current processing index and term. This does not establish persisted or recoverable snapshot contents.
facts.validity_context: Snapshot closure with nonzero lastIndex and nil callback error.
facts.recovery: Requires subsequent storage and restore paths.

facts.meaning: A first Close call starting with closed=false completed finalization, metadata writing, directory rename, applicable directory sync and snapshot reaping without a reported error. A repeated nil Close does not establish this fact.
facts.validity_context: Fallthrough success of the first-call branch, under the sink's noSync and operating-system settings.
facts.durability: Conditional on synchronization settings and unread metadata and filesystem behavior.
facts.recovery: List and Open validation remain unread.
unknowns: No concrete takeSnapshot consumer edge is asserted because adapter activation and prior Close history are unknown
closed alone does not encode completion outcome

surfaces.reason: Enqueue paths are recovered; later acceptance and completion remain partial.
Local storage reporting and report aggregation are mapped; remote report establishment remains deferred.
Observed dispatch and replacement sequence is mapped; validation and activation helpers remain unresolved.
Callbacks and coordinate updates are mapped; tuple production and full worker scheduling are not.
Coordinator and concrete sink actor are separated. Successful publication is distinguished from repeated Close return.

surfaces.entry_point: FileSnapshotStore Create, List, Open and ReapSnapshots; FileSnapshotSink.writeMeta
surfaces.reason: High-consequence frontier for determining when a snapshot becomes recoverable and when older recovery evidence is removed.
Acquired code bounds deletion by snapshot index and trailing logs, but concrete deletion semantics and restore callers need separate actor mapping.

surfaces.entry_point: NewRaft, restoreSnapshot and runtime FSM restore
surfaces.reason: Recovery entry points are identified; snapshot acceptance helpers and completion paths are incomplete.
Candidate loop is acquired, but distinct vote producers, role-transition effects and persistent context need bounded expansion.
Transport declares replication and recovery operations and constructor registers a concurrent heartbeat path. Acceptance, persistence, response validation and interaction are unread.

surfaces.entry_point: VerifyLeader, leadership transfer and user restore
surfaces.reason: API or candidate-loop evidence identifies requests; leader-side completion and authority interpretation are unresolved.
Clients provide application state transitions and snapshot content. Library callback scheduling remains inside the boundary.

surfaces.entry_point: Injected LogStore, StableStore and alternative SnapshotStore implementations
surfaces.reason: Injection is established, but built-in implementations remain within the boundary and their failure semantics cannot be externalized by assumption.
Acquired declarations describe observation channels and blocking options. Observations are not treated as proof of protocol establishment; delivery implementation remains unread.
